title: List 10 things people pay for in areas you like
builds: Picking one idea you can make a first sale with.
steps: Set a 12-minute timer.
Write four headings: Music, Marketing, Money, Beauty and self-care.
Example to get started: under Marketing, "make 5 Instagram posts a month for a local shop."
Under each heading, write things people already pay for that you could do. Aim for 10 in total. They don't have to be good yet.
Star the 3 you'd actually enjoy doing for a month.
check: You have 10 ideas, and at least one is something a person could pay you for within a month.

title: Work out profit, markup and margin
builds: Pricing your own idea so it actually makes money.
steps: Recall (1 min): without looking, write down the 3 ideas you starred yesterday.
Worked example: something costs you $2 to make and sells for $5. Profit = $3. Markup = profit ÷ cost = 3 ÷ 2 = 150%. Margin = profit ÷ price = 3 ÷ 5 = 60%.
Your turn: a custom playlist costs you $4 per client and you charge $25. Find the profit, markup and margin.
Your turn: a budget spreadsheet template costs $0.50 per sale in fees and sells for $8. Same three numbers.
Pick one of your starred ideas. Guess its cost and price, then work out the same three numbers.
check: Playlist: profit $21, markup 525%, margin 84%. Template: profit $7.50, markup 1500%, margin 93.75%.

title: Learn the map of South America
builds: Reading any region by its countries, landforms and climate.
steps: Recall (1 min): what's the difference between markup and margin? One line each.
Play the South America countries quiz once. Write down your score and time.
Look at the landforms: the Andes mountains run down the whole west side, the Amazon basin fills the north and middle, and the Atacama Desert runs along the coast of northern Chile.
Play the quiz again and beat your first score or time.
Write one sentence with your guess: why might one side of a mountain range be wet and the other side dry? You'll check it in a later task.
check: You can place Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Peru and Colombia without help. Which country is the Atacama Desert in? (Chile.)

title: See what one year of profit could grow into
builds: A rule for what you do with the money your business makes.
steps: Recall (1 min): one of your ideas makes $21 profit per client. How many clients does it take to make $500?
The difference: a business creates cash flow, which is money that comes in because of work you do. Investing puts that money somewhere it can grow without more of your time.
Watch the short Khan Academy video on compound interest.
On paper: $500 grows 7% a year. Year 1 = 500 × 1.07 = $535. Work out years 2 and 3 yourself by multiplying by 1.07 each time.
With a calculator: 500 × 1.07^10. Write down what $500 turns into after 10 years.
check: Recall: 24 clients (500 ÷ 21 = 23.8, so round up). Year 2: $572.45. Year 3: $612.52. Year 10: about $983.58, so it nearly doubles.
linkText: Khan Academy: Introduction to Compound Interest (video)

title: Fix run-on sentences in a sales message
builds: Writing an offer that people take seriously.
steps: Recall (1 min): in one line, what is the difference between cash flow and investing?
Rule: a run-on is two complete thoughts stuck together with nothing between them, or with only a comma. Fix it with a period, a semicolon, or a comma plus and/but/so.
Worked example: "I make playlists for events they fit your crowd." becomes "I make playlists for events. They fit your crowd."
Fix these: (a) "My templates save time, you just fill in your numbers." (b) "I started last month I already have two clients." (c) "Prices start at $8 they go up for custom work."
Write 3 sentences selling one of your starred ideas, then check each one for run-ons.
check: (a) "...save time. You just..." or "save time; you just..." (b) "...last month, and I already..." (c) "...start at $8. They go up..."

title: Learn your skin's three layers
builds: Understanding what skin care products can and can't do.
steps: Recall (1 min): fix this sentence: "Skin is an organ it protects your body."
Watch the TED-Ed video on skin (about 5 min).
Draw three stacked boxes and label them epidermis, dermis, hypodermis. Write one job next to each.
Zoom in on the back of your hand with your phone camera. Write down what you see: lines, pores, tiny hairs.
Write one question you now have about skin. Keep it, because it can become a future task.
check: Recall: "Skin is an organ. It protects your body." Epidermis: the outer barrier. Dermis: collagen, blood vessels, sweat glands, hair roots, nerves. Hypodermis: fat for cushioning and warmth. Skin's three jobs: protect, regulate, sense.

title: Score your 3 ideas with numbers
builds: Choosing the one idea you test first.
steps: Recall (1 min): an item costs $3 and sells for $12. What's the margin?
Make a table with your 3 starred ideas as rows and these columns: start cost ($), profit per sale ($), minutes per sale, people I could ask, enjoyment (1-5).
Fill it in with rough guesses. Guesses are fine.
Profit per hour = profit per sale ÷ minutes × 60. Work it out for each idea.
Circle the idea with the best mix of profit per hour and enjoyment. Write one sentence on why.
check: Recall: 75% ($9 ÷ $12). Example: $21 profit in 45 min = $28 an hour. You have one circled idea and a reason.

level: Level 1: Two sides of one event
title: The Berlin Conference: who was in the room?
builds: Judging any history story by asking who told it.
steps: Recall (1 min): name 3 South American countries and one landform from last Saturday.
Read the article (about 10 min). Skim the list of territories and focus on the other sections.
Make two columns: European powers in the room, and African people left out. Write 2 things each side might say about the new borders.
The article gives two views from historians. One says the conference sped up the carve-up of Africa. The other says the conference itself drew few real borders. Write one line on each view.
One sentence: why does it matter who was in the room?
check: When: Nov 1884 to Feb 1885. Who: diplomats from 14 countries. Left out: every African leader (the Sultan of Zanzibar asked to attend and was refused). About 20% of Africa was colonized before the conference and about 90% by 1890.
linkText: Al Jazeera: What happened at the Berlin Conference?

title: Count to 20 and ask a price in French
builds: Handling prices and simple conversations in French.
steps: Recall (1 min): name the three layers of skin.
Watch the video (8 min) and say each number out loud along with it.
Cover the screen and write 1 to 20 in French. Check your spelling.
Learn two phrases: "C'est combien ?" (How much is it?) and "Ça coûte douze dollars." (It costs twelve dollars.)
Say out loud the prices of three of your ideas, e.g. "Ça coûte huit dollars." Then tap Copy my week below and send it to Mom or Dad.
check: 11 onze, 12 douze, 13 treize, 14 quatorze, 15 quinze, 16 seize, 17 dix-sept, 18 dix-huit, 19 dix-neuf, 20 vingt.
